# How to Draw Mega Blastoise

Here's a step-by-step guide to drawing Mega Blastoise:

## Step 1: Basic Shapes
- Draw a large oval for the body/torso
- Add a smaller circle for the head, positioned on top
- Sketch guidelines for the limbs using simple ovals

## Step 2: Head Details
- Draw the eyes (angular, more aggressive-looking than regular Blastoise)
- Add the mouth and small nose bumps
- Sketch the ridges on top of the head

## Step 3: Shell Structure
- Draw the large, ridged shell on the back
- Add the distinctive spike/ridge patterns that run along the shell edges (Mega Blastoise has more pronounced, jagged shell edges than regular Blastoise)
- Include the segmented shell plates

## Step 4: Cannons (Key Feature!)
- Draw the two large shoulder cannons (these are bigger and more angular in Mega form)
- Add a **third cannon** coming out of the shell/back area — this is unique to Mega Blastoise
- Detail the cannon openings (dark circles/tubes)

## Step 5: Limbs
- Draw short, thick arms with three-clawed hands
- Add sturdy legs with clawed feet
- Keep proportions blocky and powerful-looking

## Step 6: Refine Details
- Add texture lines to the shell (cracks, ridges)
- Draw small spikes along the shell rim
- Add shading to show the shell's glossy, hard texture
- Include the lighter underbelly color area

## Step 7: Coloring
- Body: Blue (slightly darker/more saturated than base Blastoise)
- Shell: Brown/tan
- Underbelly: Cream or light tan
- Cannons: Dark grey or black openings

## Tips:
- Reference official artwork for accurate cannon placement
- Keep the design bulky and armored-looking
- The third cannon is the most distinguishing feature — don't forget it!
